He carried that measure into everything — the report card with the one B, then the sales target hit and immediately replaced with a higher one — and somewhere along the way he learned that what he'd done was never the thing that counted, only the gap left over. It made him very good at his work and left him with no place to stand when a number finally came in that he couldn't improve.

Precipitating. Five weeks ago, at his annual physical, the bloodwork came back with elevated liver enzymes, and when the doctor asked him point-blank how much he was drinking, he heard himself give a number half the size of the truth. A retest was scheduled for six weeks out, with instructions to cut it out in the meantime.
